title: This musical makes for a truly G’wonderful day in Brooklyn! #theatre ...
transcript: Goofy's Toxic Aquatic Adventure is a dystopian puppet musical about a mermaid-like creature from Brooklyn trying to find belonging in a future where Gowanus has been turned into a capitalist hellscape theme park, making friends with a rat, a sludge monster, and the disembodied arm of her dead mother along the way. This show, written by La Daniela, manages to blend this cartoonish whimsy with some dark, gruesome and crude content without it feeling like shock value. And conversely, they were able to pull off this grotesque, searing satire of gentrification and capitalism while still finding so much charm and heart, at the core of the story, with this lovable cast of characters. It's a show that kind of miraculously manages to have its cake and eat it too. It also riffs on some recognizable story beats from Broadway and movie musicals like Wizard of Oz, Little Mermaid and several more, with even a lot of little musical theatre easter eggs in there for people in the know. If you judge it compared to a lot of the other musical theatre happening at major theatre companies in New York, it's definitely a little rough around the edges. But I think the context of seeing it at the Bushwick Starr specifically, which is known for doing a lot of performance art and more experimental stuff, made it feel to me like a scrappy, avant garde show at its core that just kind of uses the superficial trappings of Disney-esque musicals to achieve its artistic goals. but again, still weirdly at the same time kind of capturing a lot of what makes those feel good musicals appealing. So if this sounds like your kind of thing, Gooey’s Toxic Aquatic Adventure is currently running at the Bushwick Starr until February 28th, and all of the tickets are like only $30
